svg.title: Thermodynamic sea-ice update: algorithm flow
svg.desc: One thermodynamic sea-ice step: the state (surface temperature, SST, ice thickness, snow, compactness and ice mask) gives the snow depth and the effective conductance; for resolved ice a semi-implicit surface-energy equation gives a trial surface temperature, which is cut off at the melting point (producing melt energy) only if it exceeds it, while thin ice or open water takes the SST directly, with no melting-point test, and thin ice passes the whole atmospheric flux, of either sign, on as melt energy; snow melts before ice and flooded snow is converted to ice; the ice energy ledger uses the ocean-to-ice flux returned by the slab one step earlier, which under ice is the sum of the conductive share Q_f = K_z(T_f - T_o) that the ice hands to the slab (the rest of the conduction K_z(T_i - T_o) once the part K_z(T_i - T_f) from the ice base to the surface is kept in the ledger), the deep-ocean heat flux from the three-dimensional ocean, and the freezing-point correction C_o(T_o* - T_f)/dt, which resets the slab to the freezing point so that its heat above it melts ice and a deficit grows ice; under established ice the slab already sits at the freezing point and only the deep-ocean flux remains, while over open water only the correction acts, where the SST starts the step below the freezing point; the ledger then updates the thickness, clipped to zero and to the maximum thickness, and the latent-heat flux Q_max of any thickness above the maximum is carried to the next ice step, whose surface-temperature step uses Q_a^modified = Q_a − Q_max; compactness grows or shrinks with the thickness change, is reset to zero when the ice disappears, and is thresholded into the binary ice mask; the surface temperature, snow, thickness and ice mask return to the coupler, while the compactness stays in the ice module.
